children: OpenWorld entered a non-binding term sheet with Meridian to establish a tokenized financing program of up to $1 billion to fund a solar‑powered, residential battery‑backed distributed AI computing network.
Non-binding term sheet with Meridian to create a tokenized financing program of up to $1 billion to fund purchase and deployment of the network.
OpenWorld to act as advisor, structuring agent and services provider and to administer the program on OpenWorld Enterprise.
Program assets include residential battery storage (Powerwall), solar panels and AI computing equipment; Meridian holds purchase rights and will own storage assets.
Initial deployment planned for 10,000 homes; test installs begin Q4 2026, first commercial site targeted Q1 2027.
AI inference capacity to be provided without new centralized data centers, grid interconnections or water cooling; hosts receive payments and lower‑cost electricity.
This is an AI-powered summary. It may contain inaccuracies. Consider verifying important information with the source. Please note this summary is solely based on documents filed with the SEC.

title: OpenWorld signs non-binding term sheet for up to $1B tokenized financing of solar‑powered distributed AI network
